subject: general
question: Kaveri Sankramana is a festival celebrated in ________ in the month of October.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Karnataka.__** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kaveri Sankramana** is celebrated in the month **of October.**
 
• This festival marks the **birth of the River Kaveri which originates at Talakaveri in Kodagu.**
 
• During this period, there is a precise moment when the** Sun enters the Libra Zodiac sign (Tula Raashi),** and simultaneously, the holy water springs called the **"tirtha" flows from the kundike (pond) and empties itself into the larger holy tank located at Talakaveri.**
 
• 
 
People immerse themselves in this water as they consider it to be of significant importance.

 
 
• 
 
This holy water, **known as tirtha,** is also collected in bottles and distributed among every Kodava household.

 
 
• 
 
This water is fed to the dying in the belief that they will attain** Moksha (salvation).**

 
 
• 
 
On the next day, another ritual called** Kani Puja** (worshipping mother earth) is performed.

 
 
• 
 
**Kani is considered to be the avatar of Goddess Parvati**, of which,** Goddess Kaveri** is an **incarnation.**

 
 
• 
 
Married women drape themselves in lovely silk sarees and perform rituals which include a taliyatakki bolca (an oil lamp placed on top of rice grains spread on a bell-metal plate), a vegetable wrapped in a red silk- believed to be a symbol of Goddess Kaveri, and adorned with jewelry and flowers, three betel leaves, and three areca nuts are placed on a plate.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Cauvery River (Kaveri) **originates from **Talakaveri **on the Brahmagiri range near **Cherangala village of Kodagu (Coorg) district of Karnataka.**
 
• **The total length of the river- **approximately 800 km.
 
• This holy river flows in the **south-east for 705 km** in the states of **Karnataka and Tamil Nadu**, descends the Eastern Ghats in a series of great falls.

 and then finally empties into the Bay of Bengal south of Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu after breaking into a large number of distributaries forming the delta which is often called the** “garden of southern India”.**
 
• **Total Drainage Area-** 81 thousand Sq.km.
 
• Physiographically, the basin of Kaveri can be segregated into three parts – **the Westen Ghats, the Plateau of Mysore, and the Delta.**
 
• The delta area is the **most fertile tract** in the basin.
 
• **Soil types found in the basin-** **black soils, red soils, laterites, alluvial soils, forest soils, and mixed soils**.
 
• The Karnataka section of the basin receives rainfall mainly from the S-W Monsoon and partially from N-E Monsoon while The section of the basin in Tamil Nadu receives from the North-East Monsoon.
 
• The famous **Sivasamudram Falls **are also located on the river Kaveri.
 
• **Left Bank tributaries of the River**- Harangi, the Hemavati, the Shimsha, and the Arkavati.
 
• **Right Bank tributaries of the River**: Lakshmantirtha, the Kabbani, the Suvarnavati, the Bhavani, the Noyil, and Amaravati.
